title: Selling Digital Products from Africa: My Unfiltered Take After Deploying for Hundreds of Creators
author: COREMERCH
excerpt: Selling digital products from Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Pakistan, Bangladesh, or Zimbabwe is fully operational with sovereign commerce infrastructure that has no geographic restrictions.

content.text: As a digital creator from Africa, I know firsthand the frustration of selling digital products to international buyers when platforms like Stripe, PayPal, and Gumroad are unavailable or severely restricted in my country. Nigeria, my home country, is just one of the many African nations where these platforms have been blocked or heavily censored, leaving creators with no choice but to rely on cumbersome workarounds or abandon their online businesses altogether. I've seen it happen to friends and fellow creators, and I've lived through it myself. But today, I'm here to tell you that there's a better way – a way to sell digital products without relying on those platforms, and to do so with full control over your online store and payment processing. It starts with a fundamental shift in how we think about infrastructure, and it requires a willingness to confront the uncomfortable truth about platform dependency.
The Honest Reality Most Creators Avoid

Most creators avoid talking about the true challenges of selling digital products in Africa. They downplay the impact of platform restrictions, or they pretend that workarounds like crypto payments are foolproof. But the reality is that these limitations are a major obstacle to growth, and they can be a deal-breaker for many creators who need to access international markets to succeed. By ignoring this problem or sugarcoating its severity, we're doing a disservice to our fellow creators and to the entire digital economy of Africa.
Why the Popular Advice Is Wrong

Popular advice often tells creators to rely on crypto payments or to use alternative platforms that claim to be more open. But these solutions are often shoddy workarounds that leave creators exposed to security risks, high fees, and limited scalability. They may provide temporary relief, but they don't address the underlying issue – the lack of control over our own infrastructure and payment processing. By buying into this advice, we're perpetuating a culture of dependency on platforms that don't have our best interests at heart.
What the Architecture and Experience Actually Show

At Core Merch, we've built and deployed sovereign digital commerce stacks for hundreds of creators in Africa. And what we've seen time and time again is that this approach can be a game-changer. By using infrastructure like Cloudflare, Supabase, and NOWPayments, creators can build their own online stores and payment systems, free from the constraints of traditional platforms. It's not just about avoiding platform restrictions – it's about building a scalable, secure, and customizable architecture that puts you in control.
Building a sovereign digital commerce stack means taking control of your online business and payment processing, free from the constraints of traditional platforms.
The Uncomfortable Truth About Platform Dependency

The truth is that most creators are still dependent on platforms like Stripe, PayPal, or Gumroad. They rely on these platforms for payment processing, customer support, and even marketing tools. But this dependency comes with a high cost – loss of control, higher fees, and vulnerability to platform outages and restrictions. By acknowledging this truth and taking steps to break free from platform dependency, we can build a more resilient and sustainable digital economy for Africa.
